## Endpoint and conventions

For a finite index set I and a real family V=(v_i) in R^n, Frame(V) means there exist 0<A<=B<infinity such that A||x||^2 <= sum_i <x,v_i>^2 <= B||x||^2 for every x. A strict source scaling has w_i>0 and produces sqrt(w_i)v_i, globally Parseval. Positive coefficients c_i mean multiplication by c_i, so w_i=c_i^2; these conventions are equivalent by the positive square root.

The universal conjecture quantifies over finite I, dimensions n, and indexed unit frames F,G in R^n: Sc(F)=Sc(G) and Tight(G) imply existence of a strict scaling with Fac(scaled F)=Fac(G). We exhibit I=Fin15, n=2 satisfying the hypotheses and prove the stronger assertion that for EVERY positive coefficient function c, Fac(G) is not even contained in Fac(cF). Hence this is the exact negation of the literal universal statement, with source definitions, rather than a six-subset substitute for that statement. The six subsets below witness failure only after full hypotheses are proved. Reindexing 0,...,14 to the source's 1,...,15 is a bijection transporting every subset and both posets.

## Outer-product bridge

For v=(x,y), put D(v)=(x^2-y^2,2xy), regarded as a real pair; complex notation for this pair is only real planar arithmetic. Direct multiplication gives

vv^T = (||v||^2/2)Id + (1/2)[[D(v)_1,D(v)_2],[D(v)_2,-D(v)_1]].

Thus for unit vectors and weights w>=0, their outer-product sum equals lambda Id iff sum wD(v)=0 and sum w=2lambda. For sum w>0 this has lambda>0 and supplies the frame inequalities with equality. Conversely a positive-bound tight identity supplies precisely these equations by the trace and the off-diagonal/difference-of-diagonal entries. For arbitrary positive c, D(cv)=c^2 D(v).

For each nonempty J, the source Parseval condition is therefore equivalent to 0 in conv{D(v_j):j in J}. In the forward direction trace gives sum w=2 and t=w/2 are convex coefficients. In reverse, convex coefficients t>=0 summing to one give w=2t and the identity. If that identity holds, then <x,v_j>=0 for all j would imply ||x||^2=0, so the unscaled J-family spans and is a frame: no hidden assumption of a preexisting subframe has been lost. Tightness with nonnegative coefficients and positive bound converts to Parseval by dividing every squared weight by lambda. The zero-weight family with bound zero is never accepted. Empty J has no Parseval identity in R^2 and is adjoined only by convention. A singleton of nonzero unit diagram vector has no zero convex combination.

## Exact construction and frame hypotheses

Let z=cos(2pi/15)+i sin(2pi/15), epsilon=pi/30, u=cos(epsilon)+i sin(epsilon). For j=0,...,14 set g_j=(cos(pi j/15),sin(pi j/15)); set f_j=g_j except f_0=(cos(pi/60),sin(pi/60)). The double-angle identities give D(g_j)=z^j and D(f_0)=u. All original vectors are real and unit by cos^2+sin^2=1. The determinant of g_1,g_2 is sin(pi/15)>0. These unchanged vectors span R^2 in both families. More explicitly the continuous positive function <x,g_1>^2+<x,g_2>^2 on the unit circle has a strictly positive minimum; the sum for the whole family lies above this minimum and at most 15. Homogeneity supplies the required frame inequalities for every x, including x=0.

The geometric sum S=sum_{j=0}^{14}z^j satisfies (1-z)S=1-z^15=0; z!=1, so S=0. The outer-product bridge gives sum g_jg_j^T=(15/2)Id. Hence G is tight with a strictly positive bound 15/2, not necessarily Parseval as the hypothesis allows.

## Uniform all-subset geometry

We prove the circle criterion rather than relying on a plot or an oriented-matroid slogan. For finitely many distinct unit-circle points with at least two points, define consecutive cyclic angular gaps using their increasing angles and one wrap by 2pi. A gap >pi puts all vertices in the complementary arc of length <pi, hence in an open semicircle. The middle direction has positive real dot product with every vertex, and therefore with every convex combination; their hull does not contain zero.

Conversely suppose zero is outside the hull K. The hull is compact (the continuous image of a finite coefficient simplex), so choose p in K minimizing ||p||, with p!=0. For each vertex q and 0<t<=1, p+t(q-p) is in K; expanding its squared norm and using minimality gives 2<p,q-p>+t||q-p||^2>=0. Letting t decrease to zero yields <p,q>>=||p||^2>0. Thus all vertices lie in the open semicircle centered on p. Since there are finitely many vertices, their lifted angles in that semicircle have spread strictly less than pi. Their complementary consecutive cyclic gap is >pi. We have proved 0 in K iff there is no gap >pi. If no pair is antipodal, no consecutive gap equals pi; in that case the criterion is max gap <pi. This proof does not assume a full-dimensional hull. In particular a two-point hull contains zero iff the two points are antipodal: if t a+(1-t)b=0 with unit a,b, then t=1-t and b=-a. A singleton cannot contain zero. These observations also pay all degenerate cases without a polygon-boundary assumption.

No two distinct G diagrams are antipodal: equality of their angular difference to pi modulo 2pi would give 2d=15 modulo30 for an integer d, impossible by parity. For ANY selected J of size at least two, its consecutive G gaps have form 2pi d/15 with integer 1<=d<=14, and distance from pi equals pi|2d-15|/15 >= pi/15. These are symbolic statements for arbitrary J, not an enumeration of subsets.

If 0 is not selected, F and G diagrams on J coincide. If 0 is selected, replacing its angle 0 by epsilon preserves circular order because 0<epsilon<2pi/15, the smallest possible other angle. All consecutive gaps are unchanged except the two adjacent to 0: the forward gap decreases by epsilon and the preceding wrap gap increases by epsilon. This description remains valid for two points (two distinct gaps). Their positivity is preserved and each changes in absolute value by at most epsilon=pi/30<pi/15, so its strict comparison with pi cannot change. No antipodal pair is introduced: for any pair involving 0 the original directed angular difference and its distance to pi have the same lower bound pi/15; the perturbation changes it by only epsilon. Other pairs are unchanged. Hence the circle criterion yields 0 in the G-diagram hull on J iff 0 is in the F-diagram hull on J for EVERY J with at least two points. Empty and singleton cases agree separately. The outer-product bridge gives Sc(F)=Sc(G) as actual collections of subsets of I, with the identity on indices an order isomorphism. No abstract permutation or minimal-support proxy is used.

For completeness this is not an obstruction caused just by F lacking a strict whole-frame scaling. The five disjoint triples {j,j+5,j+10}, j=0,...,4, all have gaps <pi even after the perturbation. Each triangle contains zero in its interior: the criterion gives membership; a boundary representation would put zero on one edge, which for unit points would force an excluded antipodal pair. Its barycentric coordinates are therefore all positive. Choose positive zero-diagram weights on each of these five triples and combine; then normalize by their positive total trace to obtain a strict Parseval scaling of all F.

## Simultaneous compatibility obstruction

Suppose c_i>0 and Fac(G) is contained in Fac(cF). Put w_i=c_i^2>0. Every nonempty tight subset of G must satisfy its homogeneous zero-diagram equation after scaling F, regardless of its own tight bound. No assertion that different subsets have the same bound is made.

Let omega=z^5=cos(2pi/3)+i sin(2pi/3)=-1/2+i sqrt(3)/2. It has omega^3=1, omega!=1, and 1+omega+omega^2=0, either by the geometric sum or these real coordinates. For j=1,2,3,4 the triple T_j={j,j+5,j+10} lies within 0,...,14 and omits 0. Its G-diagram sum is z^j(1+omega+omega^2)=0. It is nonempty with positive trace and hence tight. Its scaled F equation divided by z^j is

w_j + w_{j+5}omega + w_{j+10}omega^2=0.

Imaginary parts give (sqrt(3)/2)(w_{j+5}-w_{j+10})=0, and real parts then give w_j=(w_{j+5}+w_{j+10})/2. Therefore w_j=w_{j+5}=w_{j+10}. This explicitly proves uniqueness of the real triangle relation by rank two, without assuming equality of tight bounds.

Let P={0,3,6,9,12} and Q={5,8,11,14,2}=P+5 modulo15. The number eta=z^3 has eta^5=1 and eta!=1, so 1+eta+eta^2+eta^3+eta^4=0. Thus P has zero G-diagram sum and Q has z^5 times that sum; both are tight by positive trace. Consequently

w_0 u + w_3 z^3+w_6 z^6+w_9 z^9+w_12 z^12=0,
w_5 z^5+w_8 z^8+w_11 z^11+w_14 z^14+w_2 z^2=0.

The triangle identities give exactly w_8=w_3 (T_3), w_11=w_6 (T_1), w_14=w_9 (T_4), and w_2=w_12 (T_2). They cover every required substitution, including 12+5=17 congruent to2 and z^17=z^2. But w_0>0 and 0<pi/30<pi imply sin(pi/30)>0, contradiction.

Thus for every positive c there is a member of Fac(G) missing from Fac(cF). This stronger noncontainment proves the required failure of equality. If the source insists on a globally Parseval strict scaling, that class is a subclass of the positive coefficients already excluded. Conversely any globally tight positive scaling can be normalized by its common positive bound; multiplying all vectors by a common nonzero scalar preserves exactly all tight subsets because every subset bound is multiplied by its square. Therefore normalization cannot evade the contradiction.

All original real-dimension, unit, spanning, nonnegative scaling, strict positivity, squared-weight, empty-subset, positive-bound and common-index quantifiers have now been paid. No algebraic-field, generic-position, complex-frame or pairwise-antipodal hypothesis is added to the source. The no-antipodes property is proved for this chosen witness only. The same reasoning works for every diagram perturbation 0<epsilon<pi/15, with the corresponding half-angle original vector, but this is one family outcome and no additional credit claim.
